title: Twenty early box signals do not pass a later Kepler test for KIC 8462852 at 1 to 10 days
abstract: We search quiet Kepler release 25 data for short-period transit signals in KIC 8462852. Twenty box signals selected in quarters 1 to 8 do not pass a fixed later test in quarters 9 to 16. The largest later depth divided by phase-shift scatter is 1.68, below the 2.96 control threshold. The smallest family rank is 0.639. Aperture flux and two other median-filter widths give similar small later statistics. The full screen recovers 3 of 6 injected boxes at 100 ppm, 4 of 6 at 300 ppm, and 5 of 6 at 1000 ppm. A traced failure shows that phase controls can reject a recovered injected signal. This conditional null result applies to the selected periods, durations and masks. It does not exclude all planets or test the proposed long-period companion. No new planet or stable transit candidate is found. Code, aggregate results, figures, input hashes and an external-scratch retrieval recipe are included.

Tests the known 0.88-day wave in one quarter. Our test selects box signals in early quarters and checks later predictions.
Reports an independent TESS event and a tentative long-period companion. That proposal is outside our search range.
